newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan leaders to meet on May 12.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan leaders to meet on May 12.

text.p: The prime ministers of India and Pakistan will hold talks on May 12 ahead of a regional summit in the Maldives, Indian officials said on Thursday.

Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, will meet before the start of a three-day summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in the capital of the Maldives, Male.

The meeting, which had been anticipated but the date of which had not been known, would follow two rounds of high-level talks that resumed in March after three years of recriminations between the longstanding foes.

It would be the first meeting between the prime ministers of the two countries since April 1993 when Nawaz Sharif and then Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao met on the sidelines of a SAARC conference, Indian officials said.

Pakistani President Farooq Khan Leghari met Rao in May 1995, also on the sidelines of a SAARC meeting, and talked at length about Kashmir, which has been divided between the two nations since shortly after they won independence from Britain in 1947.
Peace talks had broken down in January 1994 over Kashmir, the source of two of the three wars which the countries have fought since independence.
Negotiations resumed in March between the foreign secretaries -- the highest ranking civil servants in the foreign ministries.
Gujral, who was foreign minister under his predecessor, ousted prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, met Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan on April 9.
Gujral was sworn in as prime minister 12 days later and has kept the foreign ministry portfolio in his centre-left government, vowing to pursue his efforts to improve relations with Pakistan.
At their meeting in the Maldives, Gujral and Sharif will fix the dates of a second round of talks between foreign secretaries, expected to be held in Islamabad, United News of India said.
Indian officials said the SAARC summit would focus on speeding economic cooperation and alleviating poverty.
In addition to India and Pakistan, SAARC includes Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
